title: Gallows Pass Railway
intent: A bounded railway cutting runs past derailed coaches to a tunnel. A maintenance siding path parallels the track, while a guarded trestle has a service walkway beneath its deck.

staging.logistics: Van is already staged on a prepared roadhead/service apron through expedition logistics. Travel to this remote region is a campaign transition; no new vehicle, ferry or flight gameplay is assumed.

circulation: Parallel siding prevents the entire mission becoming a single corridor. Coach interiors have two ground-supported exits; derailment does not imply mandatory climbing. Tunnel refuge cross-passage returns to the siding; trestle walkway provides a guarded secondary path.
systems: Wind through cutting, loose sheet metal, signal wiring and rail-borne sound remain ordinary baselines. There is no moving train hazard until actual telegraph and simulation support exists.
campaign: Signal register, carriage inventories and timetable contradictions form a transport case that can tie remote supply routes together without prescribing supernatural cause.
refine: Make coach orientation and end-door support physically believable; the rectangles are footprint reservations.
Engineer trestle deck, lower stairs, rail barriers and tunnel rock support; visible voids cannot be traversable ghost-only shortcuts.
Limit mission to the authored tunnel segment; a locked maintenance end is a visible world boundary, not an infinite railway.
